part: Ranked Tensor construction, broadcasting, matmul, reduction, and shape inspection
why: The application needs one checked array value and a visible shape law before model code or embedding code can be trusted.

part: Two-layer training recipe with named parameters, loss, gradient, and SGD update
why: This is the central AI training loop. The manual chain-rule fallback works, but the intended compute.gradient path is not executable across tiers.

part: Deterministic Dataset/Loader wrapper with seed, shuffle, bounded batches, and collate
why: The probe had to hand-write order shuffling and two batch constructors; this is common connective tissue for every training example.

part: Checksummed model-state save and restore with explicit file authority
why: A training run must prove that restored parameters equal the saved parameters before deployment or resume.

part: Exact embedding vector index with cosine scoring and bounded top-result scan
why: The AI application needs a small retrieval path that can serve as a correctness oracle for any later approximate index.

part: OpenAI-compatible JSON request, SSE response reader, and bounded tool-call loop
why: A provider-neutral adapter needs streaming output, tool-call detection, a tool result turn, and a hard step bound.

part: Explicit F32 GPU placement and backend receipt
why: Accelerator use must report requested and selected devices, precision profile, capabilities, and fail closed when unavailable.

part: Same-size matmul timing harness for interpreter, native Jet, and NumPy/PyTorch when installed
why: Performance claims need the same dimensions, repetitions, result check, tier, and incumbent availability record.
